definition: Exposed to public, like the demo. No credentials, no real data, no published ports beyond loopback on the operator's own machine. Anything public must be replay-safe to observe: reads only, or writes against evaporating demo state. A public endpoint that admits a real write is a defect, not a demo. Auth: none; refusals still apply.
source: coordination-protocol-contract-package spec/scopes.md at 3b9ce9b3b4e788b961e4332bfbe0949ec2d31c2e, which also names this repo in the method-to-scope map: 'demo stub | note.list, note.create | public (evaporating state only)'.

seams.state: In-memory notes, created at process start and gone at exit. note.create is a real write to a store that evaporates -- which is what lets a write live at this scope at all.
seams.auth: none, by definition of the scope

exposure.evidence: demo/server.py:123 -- ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler).serve_forever(), port from ENV PORT defaulting to 18080
exposure.note: Loopback on the operator's own machine, which is what the scope permits. Read from the server rather than restated from the method-to-scope map: rule 4 says exposure is measured, and the map is the claim being checked, not evidence for it.

invariants: No credential is required and none is accepted.
No durable store: a restart is the reset, so observing the seam cannot damage anything.
An unknown method refuses here exactly as it would at any other scope.
